problem_text:
A retail distribution center must devise a procurement and storage strategy for a crucial perishable ingredient across an upcoming 17-week schedule.  
The initial stock available at the start of the schedule is 18 kilograms.  
In each week \(t = 1, \dots, 17\), the supplier permits the center to submit a procurement request whose amount must fall between 8 and 67 kilograms.  
Nevertheless, every request placed will require 1 week for delivery before it can be utilized to meet weekly requirements or restore stock levels.  
The weekly requirement for the ingredient is provided as follows:  

* Week 1: requirement 25 kg  
* Week 2: requirement 46 kg  
* Week 3: requirement 54 kg  
* Week 4: requirement 15 kg  
* Week 5: requirement 19 kg  
* Week 6: requirement 48 kg  
* Week 7: requirement 35 kg  
* Week 8: requirement 59 kg  
* Week 9: requirement 33 kg  
* Week 10: requirement 57 kg  
* Week 11: requirement 28 kg  
* Week 12: requirement 32 kg  
* Week 13: requirement 42 kg  
* Week 14: requirement 33 kg  
* Week 15: requirement 11 kg  
* Week 16: requirement 10 kg  
* Week 17: requirement 10 kg  

Stock‑outs are tolerated, but any unsatisfied requirement will be forfeited and not carried forward.  
Throughout the entire schedule, ingredient quantities may be treated as continuous, and the total quantity of physical stock held at any moment must not surpass the cold‑storage capacity of 29 kilograms.  

In week 16, the maximum procurement amount allowed is 55 kilograms.  
In week 16, the physical stock on hand must be no less than 21 kilograms.  

The aggregate expense over the schedule comprises three elements: the procurement expense, amounting to 6 per kilogram ordered; the storage expense, amounting to 1 per kilogram of stock kept from one week to the next; and the penalty for unmet requirements, amounting to 8 per kilogram of unsatisfied weekly requirement. Determine the optimal procurement quantity for each week and monitor the resulting stock and shortage levels so as to minimize the total expense.
